definitions.explanation: The act of imitating someone's voice, mannerisms, or appearance for entertainment. A popular form of comedy in Japan, where professional impersonators mimic celebrities on television shows.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{物|もの}まねは{上手|じょうず}だ。
{忘年会|ぼうねんかい}で{社長|しゃちょう}の{物|もの}まねをして{笑|わら}われた。
examples.english: I did an impersonation of the company president at the year-end party and got laughs.

examples.japanese: テレビの{物|もの}まね{番組|ばんぐみ}で{有名|ゆうめい}になった{芸人|げいにん}も{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many comedians became famous through impersonation shows on TV.

notes:
USAGE:
Can also be written as {物真似|ものまね} in kanji. Used as a noun or with する as a verb: {物|もの}まねをする (to do an impersonation). The person who performs impersonations is called a {物|もの}まね{芸人|げいにん} or ものまねタレント.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Impersonation comedy is a major genre in Japanese entertainment. TV shows dedicated to {物|もの}まね are popular, and annual {物|もの}まね contests draw large audiences.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {物|もの}まねをする: to do an impersonation
- {物|もの}まね{芸人|げいにん}: impersonation comedian
- {物|もの}まね{番組|ばんぐみ}: impersonation show
- {物|もの}まねが{上手|じょうず}: good at impersonations
